articles.headline: Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d'Or ahead of Kylian Mbappé, Lamine Yamal; first Englishman in 25 years
articles.description: Harry Kane has become the first Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or in 25 years after beating Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal to the award in London on Saturday.
articles.headlineJa: ハリー・ケインが2026年バロンドールを受賞、キリアン・エムバペとラミン・ヤマルを抑え、イングランド人として25年ぶりの快挙
articles.descriptionJa: 土曜日にロンドンで行われた授賞式で、ハリー・ケインがキリアン・エムバペとラミン・ヤマルを上回り、イングランド人として25年ぶりにバロンドールを受賞した。
articles.body:
Harry Kane has become the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d'Or, beating Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal to claim football's most prestigious individual award.

Kane was presented with the prize -- which is organised by the magazine France Football and voted on by 100 journalists from around the world -- on Monday at a star-studded gala in London, where he was rewarded for a historic season for club and country.

The 33-eyar-old starred for Bayern Munich in the Bundesliga and the Champions League and led England to the World Cup semifinals, scoring 73 goals in the process. He is the fifth English player to ever receive the honour, and the first since Michael Owen in 2005.

"Thank you to everyone who voted for me, I can imagine it was tough, so thank you to everyone who voted for me," an emotional Kane said on stage at the London Palladium Theatre.

Rival Mbappé became the all-time top scorer in World Cup history this summer, with 22 goals, 10 of them scored at this year's edition, while Yamal won the tournament with Spain.

Members of the Ballon d'Or jury choose 10 players, in order, from a 30-player shortlist, with the award going to the player who receives the most points overall.

Kane follows Ousmane Dembélé, who won the prize in 2025, and Rodri who won it in 2024.

For the last two decades, the award was dominated by Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, who top the all-time rankings with eight and five Ballons d'Or respectively.

The Ballon d'Or is seen as the greatest individual prize in football, alongside FIFA's The Best award.

Among the other categories in Monday's ceremony, Yamal was named the Men's Young Player of the Year after starring for Barcelona in LaLiga, and for Spain at the World Cup.

"I'd have liked it to be [teammate Pau] Cubarsi," Yamal said, during a brief speech. "This prize should have been for him. He deserves it."

Spain's Luis de la Fuente won Coach of the Year after guiding Spain to the World Cup, and his first-choice keeper, Unai Simón, was named Men's Goalkeeper of the Year.

articles.headline: Giants' Cam Skattebo, John Harbaugh object to lowering helmet penalty
articles.description: Giants coach John Harbaugh and Cam Skattebo took issue with a first-quarter penalty call Sunday against Houston, when the running back was flagged for unnecessary roughness for impermissible helmet contact.
articles.headlineJa: ジャイアンツのカム・スカッテボとジョン・ハーボーがヘルメット下げの反則判定に異議
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日のヒューストン戦の第1クォーターで、ランニングバックのスカッテボが不適切なヘルメット接触による「不必要なラフネス」の反則を科されたことに対し、ジョン・ハーボーコーチとスカッテボが不満を表明した。
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- The New York Giants might have won and played their most complete game Sunday against the Houston Texans, but running back Cam Skattebo and coach John Harbaugh aren't happy with the way one play was officiated.

Harbaugh and Skattebo disagreed with a penalty call in the first quarter when Skattebo was flagged for a personal foul -- unnecessary roughness -- for impermissible helmet contact.

Skattebo was penalized for lowering his head into a defender on the first-quarter run that originally went for a 7-yard gain. It sent Houston safety M.J. Stewart flying to the ground when the two collided and left Skattebo and Harbaugh visibly upset with the call. 

Skattebo still wasn't happy after the Giants' 27-21 overtime victory, in which he had his first 100-yard rushing game. He finished with a career-high 124 yards on 17 carries.

"The NFL loves to post me [on social media] when I do stuff like that, but also wants to take stuff from me," Skattebo said Sunday. "I'm going to run the ball like I want to run the ball. And if I'm going to continue to get flagged for it or fined for it, I guess I'm going to play for free. I'm going to do what I can to be on this team and give everything I got. If they're going to punish me for that, then I'm just going to keep doing it and playing hard."

This wasn't the first time Skattebo has been called out for the infraction. He was fined $7,073 earlier this month for "illegal helmet contact on a running play."

Harbaugh was shown on the game's television broadcast vehemently objecting to the call, and was in the linesman's ear for a while after the play.

"That's how I felt about it," Harbaugh said Monday. "You can't run in there and give tacklers your chest. When you run low, your head's down there, too. You can't move your head off your shoulders. It's a physical impossibility."

The NFL has made it a point to deemphasize offensive players using their helmets as weapons. It's still rare that the infraction involves a penalty flag.

It caught Harbaugh by surprise.

"It did," he said. "It certainly did, yes."

Skattebo, the second-year running back out of Arizona State, is known for his physical style of play. He often seeks out the contact.

But Harbaugh didn't seem to think there was any kind of intent to do so with his helmet.

"I'm quite sure [Skattebo is] not trying to use his helmet as a weapon, as a battering ram. It's not the way he's thinking," Harbaugh said. "He's leading with his shoulder. That's what he's trying to do. ... So, I didn't have a problem with the technique personally at all, but we haven't heard from the league. Maybe they'll be able to enlighten us a little bit on it in terms of what they want us to teach, and that would be great."

The controversy comes one week after Skattebo saw his role greatly reduced in a loss to the New Orleans Saints. He viewed it as punishment for several costly fumbles, including late in a tie against the Washington Commanders.

articles.headline: Cardinals WR Jalen Brooks to miss rest of season with wrist injury
articles.description: Cardinals wide receiver Jalen Brooks posted on social media Monday that he will miss the rest of the season with a wrist injury.
articles.headlineJa: カーディナルスのWRジェイレン・ブルックス、手首の負傷で今季絶望
articles.descriptionJa: カーディナルスのワイドレシーバー、ジェイレン・ブルックスは月曜日、SNSを通じて手首の負傷により今シーズンの残り試合を欠場することを発表した。
articles.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. -- Cardinals wide receiver Jalen Brooks posted on social media Monday that he will miss the rest of the season with a wrist injury that needed "emergency surgery."

Coach Mike LaFleur said Brooks hurt his wrist in the first quarter but didn't mention it to anyone and continued to play.

"That sucks, man," LaFleur said. "What a tough dude.

"Then looking back at it, seeing on the tape, you could see every once in a while, I guess him kind of messing with it a little bit."

Brooks had slid into Marvin Harrison Jr.'s role as the X receiver after Harrison was traded to the Houston Texans on Oct. 11. Brooks had five catches for 81 yards, all of which came after Harrison's trade. He was on pace for a career high in yards.

LaFleur said Brooks' role will be filled by committee.

Rookie Reggie Virgil is expected to get more snaps at the X along with Kendrick Bourne and Simi Fehoko.

The Cardinals could get some help back offensively this week.

Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love is expected to practice Wednesday after missing the last two weeks of practice and the last two games with a left ankle injury. Whether Love plays Sunday is yet to be determined and will be dictated by his week of practice, LaFleur said.

LaFleur feels good about cornerback Max Melton and safety Andrew Wingard, both of whom are dealing with knee injuries, returning to practice Wednesday. Melton missed Sunday's game against the Broncos and Wingard missed the last three.

However, LaFleur does not expect defensive tackle Walter Nolen III to practice Wednesday as he continues to recover from an ankle injury that kept him out Sunday.

articles.headline: Steelers Aaron Rodgers, QB room lead NFL Week 7's best arrivals
articles.description: NFL stars continue to turn game-day arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
articles.headlineJa: スティーラーズのアロン・ロジャースらQB陣がNFL第7週の「ベスト・アライバル」を牽引
articles.descriptionJa: NFLのスター選手たちは、試合会場への到着時の装いを、毎週のファッションショーのように楽しみ続けている。
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback room set the fashion standard high Sunday in Paris, simulating European-style looks from their favorite show "Peaky Blinders" with three-piece suits and flat caps.

The idea spawned from backup quarterback Mason Rudolph, who reached out to clothing designer Mitch Purgason to have the suits custom-made for this game.

Rudolph explained that the Steelers quarterback room bonds over "Peaky Blinders." The show is extremely British, not French. But Rudolph's idea was to lean into United Kingdom experience and display with energy that they connect with personally.

Purgason said he flew up to Pittsburgh to custom-fit the Steelers quarterback room 13 days ago, then he and his associate stylist, Rachel Leskowsky, went to work making the suits in about nine days. Purgason then flew up to hand-deliver the fits last minute before their flight to Paris.

The work is worth it for looks as clean as the Steelers quarterback room. They posed for pregame pictures in Paris, and it exuded boss energy. Will this lead to more NFL positional groups leaning into translating their personal connection niche into fashion?

Here are Week 7's most fashionable NFL player gameday fits that caught our eye:

Monday night drip

Ahead of "Monday Night Football" against the Philadelphia Eagles, Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott rocked a mint green suede bomber jack for a clean look. The starting quarterback on the other side, Tanner McKee, wore a suit that included a special message -- images of his family are sewn inside his jacket.

Sunday's best

A return game for Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III on "Sunday Night Football" prompted a simple, yet sleek outfit. He wore all-white ahead of his first game against the Seattle Seahawks since signing with Kansas City in the offseason. His fellow teammates, Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce, Chris Jones and L'Jarius Sneed, all rocked suits.

It was tracksuits galore in the afternoon slate, with Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald styling a black look with a pair of shades. Meanwhile, Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby broke out a white jumpsuit, showing off his ink with an unzipped jacket.

Though Sunday marked a holiday in National Tight Ends Day, that didn't stop Rodgers and the Steelers quarterback room from channeling their inner "Peaky Blinders" in Paris with coordinated suits, boots, flat cap and all.

Thursday's looks

Caleb Williams kept it sharp ahead of "Thursday Night Football," pairing a navy suit with a black crewneck shirt. The Chicago Bears quarterback skipped the tie but not the wired earbuds. Naturally, he had his matcha drink in one hand and a structured brown leather bag in the other.

articles.headline: OKC's Jalen Williams (ankle), Cason Wallace (shoulder) to undergo surgery
articles.description: Thunder guards Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace will both be sidelined indefinitely after undergoing surgery on their ankle and shoulder, respectively.
articles.headlineJa: OKCのジェイレン・ウィリアムズ（足首）とケイソン・ウォレス（肩）が手術へ
articles.descriptionJa: サンダーのガードであるジェイレン・ウィリアムズとケイソン・ウォレスの両名が、それぞれ足首と肩の手術を受けるため、無期限で戦線を離脱する。
articles.body:
Oklahoma City Thunder starters Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace will both miss extended periods after they undergo surgery to repair injuries suffered during Sunday's win over the LA Clippers. 

Forward Williams suffered a fractured fibula and dislocated left ankle, Oklahoma City general manager Sam Presti announced Monday. Wallace suffered a torn labrum in his left shoulder, according to Presti.

Presti said the timelines for both players' return would be known after the operations. Both injuries typically require multiple months of rehabilitation, putting the availability of Williams and Wallace in doubt for the remainder of the season.

 

"We'll wrap our arms around these guys," Presti said during a news conference at the Paycom Center on Monday evening. "We'll get them back, we'll get them healthy, but we got a lot of basketball to play in front of us. We got to put it together, figure out what the next steps are because this is part of the business that we're in."

Williams suffered a gruesome injury after being fouled on a drive and landing awkwardly with 1:14 remaining in the game. His left leg collapsed, and his ankle was bent at an unnatural angle.

Medical personnel rushed to attend to him as his teammates and Clippers players reacted in shock. Oklahoma City star Shai Gilgeous-Alexander buried his face in his jersey and bent down near Williams.

Williams was placed on a stretcher and wheeled off the court to a standing ovation. He gave the crowd two thumbs up as he was taken off. Williams, 25, an All-Star and All-NBA selection two seasons ago, has had a miserable stretch of injury misfortune over the past 18 months.

Williams played the entire playoffs during the Thunder's 2025 championship run despite having a torn ligament in his right (shooting) wrist that required surgery, delivering a 40-point performance during the pivotal Game 5 win over the Indiana Pacers in the NBA Finals.

The recovery from Williams' wrist surgery caused him to miss the first 19 games of last season, and then recurring strains to both hamstrings ruined the rest of his campaign. He was limited to only 33 regular-season games and sat out 10 of Oklahoma City's 15 playoff games, exiting three other games early.

Williams is in the first season of a five-year, $239 million maximum contract that he signed in the wake of Oklahoma City's championship.

Wallace, who signed a five-year, $139 million contract extension last week, injured the shoulder in the first quarter against the Clippers. Wallace went down after running into a moving screen by Clippers center Isaiah Jackson.

Wallace, 22, an All-Defensive selection last season, moved into the starting lineup on a regular basis after Oklahoma City traded Luguentz Dort to the Atlanta Hawks in a cost-cutting move over the summer.

articles.headline: Panthers RT Taylor Moton to undergo season-ending ankle surgery
articles.description: Panthers right tackle Taylor Moton's will undergo season-ending ankle surgery while also recovering from a fractured fibula in his left leg.
articles.headlineJa: パンサーズのRTテイラー・モトン、シーズン終了となる足首の手術へ
articles.descriptionJa: パンサーズのライトタックル、テイラー・モトンは、左足の腓骨骨折からの回復と並行して、シーズン終了となる足首の手術を受ける予定だ。
articles.body:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- Carolina Panthers right tackle Taylor Moton's 2026 season will be limited to seven quarters of action.

The longtime starting lineman will undergo season-ending ankle surgery while also recovering from a fractured fibula in his left leg, coach Dave Canales said Monday.

"He's got a fracture in his fibula, up high, below the knee," Canales said. "It was really the ankle that got damaged the most with ligaments and all that. So, he'll have a procedure and that'll put him out for the rest of the year."

Moton, 32, was carted off the field during the third quarter of Sunday's 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. That exit occurred during his second game back from offseason blood clot treatment, which sidelined him from the start of training camp through the first four games of the campaign on the non-football injury list.

"We're all hurt for [Moton]," Canales said. "But we know what he represents and how he battled to get back out there."

Moton was replaced by first-round pick Monroe Freeling, who previously filled in for Moton at right tackle during the first four games of the season. Freeling, who was coming off a knee injury, gave up three quarterback pressures in 22 pass sets after replacing Moton, according to NFL Next Gen Stats.

With Freeling back at right tackle, left tackle Rasheed Walker will continue to man the blind side. The former Green Bay Packers lineman was credited with three sacks and seven total pressures allowed against Tampa Bay by NFL Next Gen Stats. One of those sacks led to a fumble by quarterback Bryce Young that was recovered by the defense for a touchdown in the 30-point blowout.

Canales was asked for an update on longtime starting left tackle Ickey Ekwonu (patellar tendon), who has been sidelined the entire season and remains on the physically unable to perform list heading into Week 8. While Canales couldn't put a timeline on Ekwonu's recovery, he did offer optimism regarding his progression following knee surgery.

"Every week seems like good milestones -- good progression," Canales said. "I can't tell you exactly how close that is, how far that is, but I know that he's trending in the right direction, getting into some more individual drills, where he can really start to load and anchor and all those things. But it's gotta get to a point where we feel really comfortable about sending somebody at him full speed and do all that. We're not quite there yet."

The Panthers have a quick turnaround ahead of their "Thursday Night Football" matchup with the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. On Monday, the team hosted a walk-through without four current starters. Left guard Damien Lewis (knee), outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips (hamstring), defensive tackle Bobby Brown III (hand) and fill-in starting cornerback Akayleb Evans (triceps/knee) were all sidelined.

Wide receiver Jalen Coker (shoulder) -- who was limited -- and Young -- who was a full participant -- were also on the projected injury report.

articles.headline: Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace injured: What's next for the OKC Thunder?
articles.description: The Thunder will be without two starting guards for months. Could they make a trade to try to replace Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace?
articles.headlineJa: ジェイレン・ウィリアムズとケイソン・ウォレスが負傷：OKCサンダーの次なる一手は？
articles.descriptionJa: サンダーは数ヶ月にわたり、先発ガード2名が欠場することになる。ジェイレン・ウィリアムズとケイソン・ウォレスの穴を埋めるため、トレードに踏み切るのだろうか？
articles.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder lost two starters to long-term injuries in their 108-101 win over the LA Clippers on Sunday night.

General manager Sam Presti announced Monday that guard Jalen Williams will undergo surgery for a dislocated left ankle and fractured fibula, while guard Cason Wallace will undergo surgery for a torn labrum in his left shoulder. Both players are expected to miss several months.

Williams was placed on a stretcher and wheeled off the court after he was injured on a drive to the basket late in the fourth quarter. Wallace left the game in the first quarter and didn't return.

They're both big losses for the Thunder, who were counting on Williams to get back to his All-Star form from the 2024-25 season and Wallace to step into the starting lineup. Williams missed 49 regular-season games last season while recovering from surgery on his right wrist and then injuring both hamstrings. He played in just five games -- and 107 total minutes -- in the postseason as OKC was beaten by the San Antonio Spurs in seven games in the Western Conference finals. Wallace signed a five-year, $139 million contract extension just before the season began.

How bad do these injuries hurt the Thunder, who are 3-0 and believe they have the talent to make it back to the NBA Finals? Do they have flexibility to make a move to replace Williams or Wallace? ESPN's reporters and analysts weigh in:

What was the early word on Williams' injury inside the Thunder?

Emotional devastation, as evidenced by Shai Gilgeous-Alexander tearing up on the court.

It's gut-wrenching any time a player suffers a gruesome injury, but hearts are especially heavy for Williams in Oklahoma City. This is a young star who has had horrific injury luck despite doing everything right in terms of conditioning and rehab. 

Williams' performance during the 2025 title run -- toughing it out with a shooting wrist that required surgery and still delivering 40 points in pivotal Game 5 of the NBA Finals -- will always be legendary in Oklahoma City. His injury misfortune has been miserable since with recurring hamstring strains that robbed him of most of last season and this cruel twist a week into this season.

The Thunder are a tight-knit team that has had to deal with the emotional consequences that come with the business of basketball. It stung to see title-winning teammates Luguentz Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins traded in salary-slashing deals. This injury causes a deeper pain that the Thunder will have to process while figuring out how to fill a massive hole in the lineup. -- Tim MacMahon

How big of a hole will these losses leave for Oklahoma City?

These two injuries are the most important development of the new season's first week in terms of how they change the championship picture. The Thunder still have excellent depth and star power at the guard and center positions, but they already shed a fair amount of perimeter depth over the summer by trading Dort, Wiggins and Joe. articles.headline: Ex-Cowboy Dez Bryant calls out police investigation after he's cited for assault
articles.description: Dez Bryant is calling for a thorough investigation by Texas' Southlake Police Department of an incident that resulted in him receiving a citation for assault.
articles.headlineJa: 元カウボーイズのデズ・ブライアント、暴行罪の召喚を受け警察の捜査に異議を唱える
articles.descriptionJa: デズ・ブライアントは、自身が暴行罪の召喚を受けることとなった事件について、テキサス州サウスレイク警察署による徹底的な捜査を求めている。
articles.body:
Former Dallas Cowboys wide receiver Dez Bryant is calling for a thorough investigation by the Southlake (Texas) Police Department of an incident Sunday that resulted in him receiving a citation for assault.

Bryant, 37, told Outkick that he confronted two drivers in a parking lot of a Mexican restaurant after they allegedly cut him off in traffic Sunday. He told the media outlet that he wanted to tell them to drive safer but that when an argument ensued with one of the men, whom Bryant described as a young adult, that driver insinuated that "he'll shoot me or whatever." Bryant told Outkick that he told the man that if he pulled out a gun, "You better use it, because if you don't, I'm going to do something to you."

Bryant, however, said the man never produced a weapon and instead took out his cellphone to record him. Bryant proceeded to knock the phone out of the man's hand.

The man then called police, which Bryant said he encouraged because he believed they would investigate the alleged threat against him.

When police arrived, an officer ordered all three men to the ground at gunpoint and put them in handcuffs. Bryant's girlfriend later came to the scene with his two daughters and recorded the incident. Bryant provided the video to Outkick.

"I was really more so concerned about my children, you know, looking at their dad, you know, being on the ground with a gun pointed at me," Bryant told Outkick.

Southlake Police spokesperson Capt. Blas Hernandez said in a news release that officers arrived at the scene with their weapons drawn because 911 calls indicated there was "a possible weapon" at the scene. He said the officers' approach to the scene was a "precaution to address any potential threats and ensure the safety of everyone at the scene."

"No firearms were recovered at the scene," Hernandez said.

Bryant told Outkick that officers only viewed the man's recording and didn't review surveillance footage -- including from the traffic incident -- and that only he received a citation from police.

According to an online record, Bryant was cited for assault by contact, with an initial hearing set for Nov. 20. The citation carries a fine of $367.

Bryant called the police investigation at the scene "very one-sided" and said one officer told him that he should be "the bigger person."

Bryant said he reached out to Outkick because, "My reputation mean everything to me."

"Treat everybody fair. Treat everybody fair. Treat everybody with respect," Bryant said when asked by Outkick what he wants from police. "Do your due diligence on what's actually going on."

Bryant, who last played in the NFL in 2020, was a three-time Pro Bowl selection during his nine-year career. He still ranks first all time in Cowboys franchise history in touchdown receptions (73), fourth in receptions (531) and sixth in receiving yards (7,459).

articles.headline: PSG beat Lyon in rescheduled match to top Ligue 1
articles.description: Senny Mayulu and Mika Godts both came off the bench to score late goals as Paris Saint-Germain moved top of Ligue 1 with a 2-0 win over Lyon on Monday.
articles.headlineJa: PSG、延期試合でリヨンを下しリーグ・アン首位に浮上
articles.descriptionJa: 月曜日に行われたリヨンとの試合で、パリ・サンジェルマンは2-0で勝利し、リーグ・アンの首位に立った。セニー・マユルとミカ・ゴッツが共に途中出場から試合終盤にゴールを決め、勝利に貢献した。
articles.body:
Senny Mayulu and Mika Godts both came off the bench to score late goals as Paris Saint-Germain moved top of Ligue 1 with a 2-0 win over Lyon on Monday.

After Lyon had dug in to frustrate PSG during a goalless first half, substitute Mayulu eventually broke the deadlock 18 minutes left when he drilled a low shot inside the near post from the edge of the box.

Godts added a second in the 84th minute following another swift counter-attack as Luis Enrique's side secured fifth straight league win, which puts them a point ahead of Rennes.

The match at Parc des Princes had been originally scheduled for Sunday, but was a postponement of 24 hours was ordered by the police as the French capital braced for more violent protests and disorder.

Before kickoff, PSG fans had unfurled a huge banner along the Auteuil Stand with the words "Kvara, the red and blue people are with you" in support of winger Khvicha Kvaratskheli, who is set for a long-term layoff after rupturing his anterior cruciate ligament in the 4-2 Champions League win over Barcelona last week.

The Ballon d'Or awards were being handed out in London as the game unfolded, with Luis Enrique a nominee for coach of the year after leading PSG to a second-straight Champions League title in 2026. However, the award went to Spain coach Luis de la Fuente.

However, Luis Enrique and PSG did receive an award at the annual gala when they were named the team of the year later in the ceremony.

Luis Enrique's side made a bright start as Lyon keeper Dominik Greif was forced into a reflex save with his foot to clear Ferran Torres' low strike off the line.

Lyon, who could also have finished the night top with a victory, went close in the 31st minute when Zachary Athekame's low, curling shot was pushed behind by PSG keeper Matvey Safonov.

The European champions stepped things up again heading towards halftime, as Maghnes Akliouche's angled drive was parried by Greif at the near post.

PSG continued to press early in the second half as first João Neves sent an acrobatic bicycle kick over and Vitinha then saw his rising shot saved.

Grief was in the right position again as the hour approached to block Torres' angled drive with his feet.

Lyon then tested Safonov again with Moussa Niakhate's header from a corner.

Luis Enrique looked to spark his side with more changes after 65 minutes, as Mayulu replaced Torres and Lucas Hernández came on for Warren Zaïre-Emery.

The substitutions had the desired impact when Mayulu broke the deadlock after 72 minutes.

Hernandez got away down the left and laid the ball off to Godts, who fed Mayulu at the edge of the penalty area, from where the 20-year-old drilled a low shot back past Grief inside the near post.

PSG made sure there would be no late drama when Godts curled in a second from the edge of the box with six minutes left following another swift counter-attack.

Information from PA was used in this recap.

articles.headline: Man United head coach Michael Carrick leaves Carrington amid doubts over his future
articles.description: Michael Carrick has left Carrington after Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox held talks over his future.
articles.headlineJa: マンUのマイケル・キャリック監督、進退を巡る不透明感の中でキャリントンを去る
articles.descriptionJa: 批判を浴びているマイケル・キャリック監督は、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドのオマール・ベラーダCEOとジェイソン・ウィルコックス・フットボール・ディレクターが進退について協議した後、キャリントンに到着した。
articles.body:
Under-fire head coach Michael Carrick has left Carrington after Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox held talks over his future.

The popular former Red Devils midfielder not only steadied the ship after Ruben Amorim's rocky reign but helped it change course as his January arrival inspired the side's rise to third in the Premier League.

Carrick's impressive stint saw him rewarded with a two-year deal to stay on as United boss, but just five months later he is facing the sack following Sunday's 3-0 Old Trafford loss to Bournemouth.

Talks over the managerial situation followed that defeat and continued after Berrada and Wilcox arrived at the Carrington training complex on Monday morning, the Press Association understands.

Carrick arrived at the training ground shortly before 2 p.m. as United Under-21s took on Hull -- the side that helped ensure United got their Premier League season off to a nightmare start -- in a behind closed doors friendly, and left at around 5 p.m.

Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann are potential replacements for Carrick, sources told ESPN.

Carrick's side are without a win in eight games after being beaten by Bournemouth days after the 4-1 Champions League loss at Como.

United have won just two of their 12 matches in all competitions this term and their seven-point return from eight matches represents their worst start to a season since 1986.

The side sit just a point above the Premier League relegation zone in 16th place ahead of Saturday's trip to Chelsea, before heading into the international break with home games against Roma and Aston Villa.

Carrick sidestepped questions over his future following the Bournemouth defeat but appeared to know the writing was on the wall as he waved to the crowd and patted his chest as he exited the pitch, with fans supportively chanting his name.

The Old Trafford faithful's anger was instead aimed at the Glazers, co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Ineos set-up, including United director of football Wilcox.

Players were booed at the final whistle and then fiercely as they followed Carrick down the tunnel on a day when the manager left skipper Bruno Fernandes on the bench.

- Sources: United consider Howe, Nagelsmann to replace under-fire Carrick

- Man United are in crisis (again), but where are the Glazers?

- Man United are stuck with their underperforming players no matter who's manager

The 32-year-old has been a pale imitation of the player who won last season's Professional Footballers' Association and Football Writers' Association awards, with the frustrated captain questioning the manager's tactics after the Como defeat.

Carrick claimed it was a "pure football" decision before the match rather than punishment but decided against giving him a minute.

Fernandes was also at Carrington on Monday -- a day off for the players -- to receive what is understood to be pre-planned treatment.

articles.headline: Magic's Jalen Suggs out at least 2 weeks with knee injury
articles.description: Magic guard Jalen Suggs suffered a mild bone bruise in his right knee and will miss at least the next two weeks.
articles.headlineJa: マジックのジェレン・サグス、膝の怪我で少なくとも2週間欠場
articles.descriptionJa: マジックのガード、ジェレン・サグスが右膝に軽い骨挫傷を負い、少なくとも今後2週間は欠場する見込みだ。
articles.body:
Orlando Magic guard Jalen Suggs will miss at least the next two weeks after suffering a mild bone bruise in his right knee, the team announced Monday.

Suggs will be re-evaluated in two weeks, but has avoided any major structural damage.

The noncontact injury occurred late in the fourth quarter of Sunday's win over the New York Knicks.

Suggs was on a breakaway fast break when his right knee appeared to buckle on his layup attempt with 2:09 remaining. Suggs stayed on the floor for several moments in pain before being helped to his feet.

He walked gingerly to the Magic's locker room with help from team personnel.

Suggs, the fifth pick in the 2021 draft, has averaged 12.6 points, 3.8 assists and 3.4 rebounds over his six-year career. He battled injuries the past two years that limited him to 92 games.

Information from ESPN's Vincent Goodwill was used in this report.

articles.headline: Virgil van Dijk: No one can replicate Mohamed Salah but new-look Liverpool attack has to step up
articles.description: Liverpool's revamped forward line has done well enough to ensure Mohamed Salah's name has never been mentioned at Anfield this season but captain Virgil van Dijk knows the next generation still have work to do.
articles.body:
Liverpool's revamped forward line has done well enough to ensure Mohamed Salah's name has never been mentioned at Anfield this season but captain Virgil van Dijk knows the next generation still have work to do.

Sunday's 2-0 win over Brighton was the first game in which Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz -- £364 million ($487m) of talent acquired over the last two summers -- and Cody Gakpo looked like they clicked together.

And they still had exciting 18-year-old England winger Rio Ngumoha, their gamechanger in their previous two matches, to bring off the bench.

Isak found the net for the sixth time in his last six league matches with an assist from Barcola after a deflected Wirtz shot had broken the deadlock, while there were several passages of play in which they appeared to be getting to grips with the new dynamic.

Salah departed in the summer, having cut his contract short by a year, after a disappointing campaign and although he left behind a wealth of goalscoring records -- and has scored 10 in 10 for new club Trabzonspor -- there is a general acceptance that everyone has moved on and no one is pining for the 34-year-old.

"I think it is the reality. What Mo has done for so many years as a winger, I don't think anyone can replicate that," van Dijk said.

"Hopefully it is going to happen but what he did was incredible. The same goes with Sadio [Mane] and Bobby [Roberto Firmino].

"Hopefully that is going to happen again and that is what we work for but now it is time for others and others have to step up.

"We can always think it was better back in the day but that is not the mentality that it should be at a club like Liverpool and I don't feel it has ever been.

"The club will always move on at a certain point and there are always players who will shine and perform for the club.

"It is down to these players who are here now to show it every three or four days.

"The second goal was class but there are plenty of moments already this season that they have been very good.

"At a club like Liverpool you have to do it every three or four days. That is always the challenge, but it is a nice challenge. I'm pretty confident that it is going to be fine."

Victory moved Liverpool, whose only defeat has come at home to Manchester City, into the Premier League's top four with a fourth clean sheet of the season.

- Iraola era at Liverpool finally has liftoff thanks to big-money forwards

- Brighton's Fabian Hürzeler digs at Liverpool - 'one team' tried to create

- Jermaine Pennant rescued by pet after dog attack: 'He saved my life'

A restructured defence has seen on-loan Barcelona defender Ronald Araujo become an instant hit on the right, while £60m ($80m) arrival from Rennes, Jérémy Jacquet, aged just 21, is looking an astute signing.

"He [Jacquet] is doing very well," van Dijk added.

"He just has to keep going and let's see where the ceiling will be. I don't think it is there yet, so keep going."
